simple.meaning: פְּנִימָה (pᵉnîymâh) is a Hebrew action word meaning “faceward , i.e. indoors.” BibleIQ anchors the English reading to this source verb before comparing its uses.
simple.biblicalBackground: This action appears 13 times in Leviticus, 1 Kings, 2 Kings, 2 Chronicles, Psalms, and 1 more, beginning at Leviticus 10:18. The surrounding contexts include blood, covenant, kingship.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to פְּנִימָה (H6441) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Actions in Scripture show what people do, what God does, and how covenant faithfulness or rebellion is described. BibleIQ compares the action across its occurrences.
simple.summary: פְּנִימָה (pᵉnîymâh) / H6441 is traced through Leviticus 10:18, 1 Kings 6:18, 1 Kings 6:19, 1 Kings 6:21 with source-language evidence and verse context.

definitions.full: H6441. penimah לִפְנִים 1Kin 6:29 see below מָּנִי֫מָה . מְּנִ֫ימָה adverb ( ה locative) 1 towards the (in-)side . 2 within (literally faceward , from point of view of one entering by opposite door); — of a building, usually temple: 1 after verb of motion Lev 10:18 ; 2Chr 29:18 , and (after הִגִּיד ) 2Kin 7:11 , also ׳לִפ Ezek 41:3 ; 2Chr 29:16 . 2 ׳פ 1Kin 6:18 , also ׳לִפ 6:30 , so read also 6:29 (for מִלִּפְנִים ᵑ0 , see Kmp Kau Kit Benz), Ezek 40:16 (twice in verse), also Psa 45:14 ᵑ0 , i.e. within the house, but Krochm Gr Che and others (plausibly) מְּנִינִים , q. v.; ׳מִמּ 1Kin 6:19 , 21 .= 2Chr 3:4 .
